messages:
max: Heads-up — saw a p99 tail spike from host egress this morning (~70ms increase) on short-chat workload. p50 is fine. Anyone else?

anya: Yea saw alerts ~09:12 UTC. Correlates with many small requests (<128B) and a burst of HTTP/2 WINDOW_UPDATE churn.

sam: I profiled a few servers. Looks like the egress fragment scheduler is slicing streams into many small frames and doing extra memcpy on host. Perf top snippet below (stripped):
```
  25.4%  runtime  egress_frag_scheduler
  12.1%  libc    memcpy
   9.8%  runtime  token_preparse
   7.2%  runtime  kvcache::evict
```

perf-bot: trace summary: 1.8M fragments/s, avg frag size 960 bytes, kv eviction rate jumped x3 during burst.

olivia: Also saw kvcache miss storms — interleaving short jobs with long decodes seems to kick off evictions. If the host path forces GPU fallback for small-kernel, we lose KV locality.

anya: Narrowing: kernel selector currently chooses small-kernel when fragment <= 2KB. Small-kernel path doesn't use device-side KV aggregation (intent was lower latency). But when fragments are many, host work outweighs benefits.

max: Ran a quick canary locally: bumped frag_threshold -> 4096 so small fragments get merged into medium-kernel path. p99 improved ~50ms for the short chat trace. CPU on host increased ~12%.

sam: Canary stats (short):
```
before: p99=210ms, host_cpu=62%
after:  p99=160ms, host_cpu=74%
kv_evictions/sec: before=120 -> after=30
```

olivia: Nice. That suggests KV eviction thrash was the main tail cause. But CPU increase might bite on dense boxes.

anya: Options: 1) dynamic threshold per-connection based on recent frag size histogram; 2) opportunistic coalescing in ingress: hold tiny writes for up to 2ms to allow batching; 3) try to make small-kernel path keep lightweight KV aggregation on device (harder).

max: I prefer (1) + (2) as low-risk. (3) is attractive but touches kernel code and model of device memory management.

sam: I implemented a simple dynamic heuristic in a fork: compute EWMA of frag_size and pick kernel+slice that minimizes expected host memcpy + eviction cost. Quick bench: improves p99 and keeps host_cpu up only ~6%. Will open PR.

olivia: For ingress coalesce: a 2ms defer for sub-256B writes can batch ~30-40% of them in traces. I'd make it opt-in per-customer (low-latency customers can keep off).

perf-bot: NOTE: add metric kvcache.evictions_per_conn and egress.frag_size_ewma.

anya: Action items:
- sam: PR with dynamic frag heur (include microbench and canary config)
- olivia: PR for 2ms coalesce configurable flag on proxy
- max: add perf counters & Grafana panels for evictions/fragments and schedule canary rollout

sam: will tag eng-runtime in the PR and include raw perf output and stair-step canary plan.

max: Let's meet quick at 10:30 to review metrics and decide rollout windows. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
